Article Title: 'Bound to breed contempt for law': SC judge Bhuyan on police action at Jantar Mantar protest
Article Text:

Poll Vote & Share your view In your opinion, should there be a review of police conduct during protests? Yes, it should be mandatory. No, it's not necessary. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan criticised police officers over the alleged assault on protesting students during the NEET agitation at Jantar Mantar and said that the detachment expected of officials appears to be disappearing.While speaking at the launch of former secretary (security) Yashovardhan Azad's book "Policing the Republic", Justice Bhuyan said that police must maintain their credibility because people seek their help when they feel wronged."All of us are dismayed when we see young officers of the Indian Police Service personally going and assaulting protesters and demonstrators. This is something very, very distressing to observe. The detachment expected of police officers somehow seems to be disappearing, and this is indeed a matter of grave concern," Justice Bhuyan said."For most common people, a policeman on the street wearing a whistle and a lathi represents the power and authority of the state. When they feel wronged, they seek the help of the police. It is, therefore, of utmost importance that the police force maintains its credibility.It can do so only by strictly adhering to the Constitution, by functioning as a truly professional force, acting impartially, displaying courage and acting with conviction, maintaining integrity and adhering to secular principles, thereby upholding the rule of law," he said.The Supreme Court judge further said that if government functionaries become lawbreakers, it is bound to breed contempt for the law and encourage lawlessness."If the functionaries of the government become lawbreakers, it is bound to breed contempt for the law and will encourage lawlessness. No civilised nation can permit that to happen. Does a citizen shed his fundamental right the moment a policeman arrests him?" Justice Bhuyan said.The alleged use of force by Delhi Police during the July 20 student protests at Jantar Mantar and the march towards Parliament has come under the Supreme Court's scrutiny, with the court constituting a high-level panel to examine complaints of excessive force.The panel, headed by former Supreme Court judge Justice R Subhash Reddy, will investigate allegations against Delhi Police and examine evidence including CCTV footage and videos of the protests.Among the allegations to be examined are the use of lathis, tear gas, pellet guns and electronic batons, as well as claims of targeted harassment and molestation of women protesters.
Article Summary: Supreme court judge justice ujjal bhuyan criticised police officers over the alleged assault on protesting students during the neet agitation. He said that the detachment expected of officials appears to be disappearing. The alleged use of force by delhi police during the july 20 student protests at jantar mantar and the march towards parliament has come under the supreme court's scrutiny.

Article Title: India, Belgium deepen defence, clean-energy ties; to double trade
Article Text:
India and Belgium signed deals to deepen defence and clean-energy ties and agreed to double bilateral trade

New Delhi: India and Belgium signed deals to deepen defence and clean-energy ties and agreed to double bilateral trade within five years as PM Modi held talks with Belgian counterpart Bart De Wever, the first Belgian PM to visit India in nearly two decades, reports Sachin Parashar.Following the talks, Modi pitched India's 7.8% growth in the last quarter as an opportunity for the world. In a joint statement with De Wever, Modi said global conflicts were causing major upheaval, disrupting food, fuel and supply chains, and creating uncertainty across sectors."Today, India's growth story is becoming a source of confidence and new opportunities for the world," said Modi.PM Narendra Modi announced a mechanism to fast-track investment between the two countries.Belgium accounted for $4.2bn of FDI inflows from April 2000 to Dec 2025, making it the 18th-largest source of FDI into India. De Wever’s visit resulted in 10 major outcomes — five MoUs, including two to boost indigenous defence manufacturing, co-design and co-development, and another five announcements, including appointment of a defence attache in Indian embassy in Brussels.Asked whether there was any discussion on pending extradition of fugitive Mehul Choksi, who remains in a Belgium jail, MEA secretary Sibi George said law enforcement cooperation was an “important topic of discussion and an important aspect of the relationship with Belgium”.“All issues of concern and interest are discussed at all levels of our engagement ... India remains committed to ensuring that fugitives are brought back to the country to face the law,” he added.Modi said ties with Belgium had expanded beyond traditional sectors. “Defence and security cooperation is a key pillar of our relationship. Today, we agreed to enhance military exchanges and training cooperation between the two countries,” said the PM. “The agreements between our govts and defence industries will open up opportunities for defence co-development and co-production. We will also further strengthen intelligence sharing and cooperation between our agencies to combat crime,” he added.PM said unprecedented cooperation, including the recently concluded FTA between India and EU – two of the world’s largest democratic blocs – would give a boost to global stability, development and shared prosperity.The leaders also discussed Ukraine and West Asia, underlining their support for the rule of law, dialogue and diplomacy. In a joint statement, they stressed the importance of ensuring the safety and security of maritime routes and maintaining safe and unimpeded maritime shipping.“Whether it is Ukraine or West Asia, we support all efforts aimed at an early end to conflicts and the restoration of peace,” the PM added.The leaders called for closer partnerships in semiconductor technologies to create resilient and advanced technology ecosystems in both countries, with Modi saying that Belgium’s expertise in semiconductors and India’s scale complement each other.The two leaders agreed to soon conclude a migration and mobility agreement to facilitate talent mobility.Belgium also expressed solidarity with India in the fight against terrorism. De Wever condemned the attack on civilians at Pahalgam in April 2025. “Both leaders underscored their commitment to a comprehensive/global approach to counterterrorism and affirmed that terrorism, in any form and manifestation and anywhere, could never be justified and called for its perpetrators to be held accountable in accordance with the law,” said the statement.The leaders also focused on clean energy, critical minerals and reliable supply chains. “The MoU on Renewable Energy signed today will give momentum to our sustainability cooperation. In critical minerals, we have decided to enhance ties in processing & recycling,” PM said.
Article Summary: India and belgium signed deals to deepen defence and clean-energy ties. Pm narendra modi announced a mechanism to fast-track investment between the two countries. De wever’s visit resulted in 10 major outcomes — five mous, including two to boost indigenous defence manufacturing, co-design and co-development.

Article Title: Watch: 2 workers make it out alive 9 days after Nepal floods hit hydropower tunnel
Article Text:
The rescue of two workers have revived hope for hundreds of others still said to be trapped

Poll Vote & Share your view What should be prioritized in Nepal's recovery plan? Rescuers in Nepal pulled two workers alive from a tunnel at the Trishuli 3A hydropower project on Friday, nine days after devastating floods and landslides trapped hundreds of workers inside tunnels across several hydropower sites.The rescue brought a dramatic breakthrough to a desperate operation, but hopes of finding more survivors rose further after rescuers heard voices coming from inside the tunnel, according to Bipin Regmi, police chief in the flood-hit district of Nuwakot.“Rescuers heard voices,” Regmi told CNN, adding that a medical team was on its way to the site.The two workers were pulled out in quick succession from inside the Trishuli 3A plant, where rescuers have been boring into a tunnel in an effort to reach 42 workers who had remained unaccounted for.Video showed about a dozen rescuers pulling one man through a small opening in the ground and clapping as he emerged. The mud-covered worker was then carried away on a rescuer’s shoulder, while a medical team checked on him.Nepal Army spokesperson Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet confirmed the first rescue during the operation. Nepal lawmaker Shri Ram Neupane later said a second worker had also been rescued alive.The tunnel leading to the underground powerhouse is more than 4 kilometres (2.5 miles) long.Dozens of workers were inside when the catastrophic flooding hit the area.About 900 workers are missing from 12 hydropower projects in Nepal, according to local authorities, with roughly 500 believed to be trapped inside tunnels. Among those unaccounted for are workers from China, South Korea and India.Read more: Nepal estimates $2.56 billion flood damage, faces $52.6 million recovery cost The rescue effort has continued under treacherous conditions since Aug. 26, when massive floods and landslides tore through parts of Nepal, likely after a glacier collapse. At least 1,259 people have been killed and more than 5,000 remain missing, according to Nepal’s disaster management agency.On the Tibet side of the border, China said late Wednesday that 21 people had been killed and 541 were missing.The chances of finding survivors have become increasingly uncertain with each passing day. Indian Army Colonel Parikshit Mehra, who was involved in the rescue operation at the Trishuli 3A site, said earlier this week that the first 48 hours are the most crucial in a tunnel rescue.“People who are stuck tend to panic much more than when they are outside in the open,” Mehra told CNN’s Anderson Cooper.“Getting stuck in a tunnel you can’t see anything. Generally if you stay in the dark you get disoriented in about 24-25 hours,” he said.“Beyond that, (after) 48 hours, you start hallucinating. And then I think from there on it’s always a fight.”Yet, even as the operation entered its ninth day, Mehra offered a note of hope saying, “There have been miracles.”Also read: Nepal minister goes back on flash flood 'compensation' claim The flash floods, triggered by an ice-rock avalanche near the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26, caused widespread destruction across northern and central Nepal, killing at least 1,282 people and leaving thousands missing. Nepal Police said the highest number of recovered bodies were reported from Chitwan, Nawalparasi East and West, Nuwakot and Rasuwa, with rescue and recovery operations continuing across the affected areas.
Article Summary: Rescuers in nepal pull two workers alive from a tunnel at the trishuli 3a hydropower project. The rescue brought a dramatic breakthrough to a desperate operation, but hopes of finding more survivors rose further. At least 1,259 people have been killed and more than 5,000 remain missing.

Article Title: Estonia minister quits after €70-million Ukraine shell deal involving Indian firm
Article Text:
Estonia minister quits in India-linked row

Estonia’s defence minister Hanno Pevkur has resigned over an arms deal to supply artillery shells to Ukraine using €70 million in European Union funds and involving Indian company, Euronews reported.It emerged on Wednesday that Estonia had paid the amount upfront for the shells, but the Indian company Neco Defence Munitions involved had no previous record of selling artillery ammunition.Estonian newspaper Eesti Ekspress reported that in 2024, Estonia signed a shell-supply deal with Italian-registered Datasel, owned by Indian company Neco Defence Munitions.Neither company had previously manufactured shells.The 2024 deal is now being challenged by Estonia in an arbitration case.Pevkur, who has been defence minister since 2022, said he was taking political responsibility for the controversy.“Although the minister does not count socks and ammunition or conduct contract negotiations, the National Audit Office’s criticisms, primarily concerning the activities of the Defence Forces and the Centre for Defence Investments, raise the question of political responsibility,” Pevkur said.The minister said he had not read the contracts, as defence ministers do not usually handle individual arms deals.“The defence minister does not conduct contract negotiations. The defence minister does not count socks and ammunition,” Pevkur said, adding: “The defence minister makes the fundamental decision to support Ukraine.”Pevkur’s resignation comes as the Russia-Ukraine war has already lasted longer than World War I, with no clear signs of peace or a return to normalcy.
Article Summary: Estonia’s defence minister hanno pevkur has resigned over an arms deal to supply artillery shells to ukraine using €70 million in european union funds. It emerged on wednesday that estonia had paid the amount upfront for the shells, but the indian company involved had no previous record of selling artillery ammunition.

Article Title: Hours after AAIB report, AI sacks Phuket flight pilot
Article Text:
Air India Friday sacked the pilot-in-command of its badly rattled Aug 4 Phuket-Delhi

Software malfunction or manual intervention? Final report may reveal

NEW DELHI: Air India Friday sacked the pilot-in-command of its badly rattled Aug 4 Phuket-Delhi flight hours after Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau's preliminary report concluded the "PIC was found non-negative for psycho-active substance in the confirmatory (dope) test". Terming this confirmation a "serious concern", AAIB has asked Directorate General of Civil Aviation to "take appropriate actions as deemed fit to prevent abuse of psychoactive substance" on "priority" in its interim safety recommendations and conclusion. Aviation secretary Samir Sinha had soon after this accident asked DGCA chief Vir Vikram Yadav to make dope rules more stringent.AI was considering action, including termination, against the PIC for some weeks now but was awaiting AAIB's prelim report into what has now been categorised as an "accident" due to its severity and impact. An AI spokesperson said: "Safety remains AI's highest priority. In line with AI's zero-tolerance approach to violation of safety, fitness or regulatory requirements, the pilot's employment has been terminated with immediate effect. "When the badly rattled Airbus A320 had landed in Delhi with 24 injured people and a damaged aircraft cabin, both the pilots were subjected to post-flight breath-analyser examination as per standard protocol.They cleared that test.But for some reason which may be disclosed in the final report, the unusual step of conducting dope tests was taken in this case. “The sample of PIC was found non-negative. Blood samples of both the flight crew were sent to path lab for confirmatory (dope) test. The confirmatory test report of PIC was found non-negative whereas the sample of co-pilot was found negative in both the tests,” stated the interim report.An AAIB probe is on to find what caused the Airbus A320 to suffer an extremely rare failure of all three hydraulic systems within seconds. The final report is expected to reveal whether it happened due to something going wrong with the aircraft’s hardware or software or whether due to some manual intervention with the PIC having some role in that, if any. Hydraulics on an Airbus A320 use pressurised liquid to move heavy flight controls, lower the landing gear, and stop the wheels.Such was the impact of this “event” which happened that 24 people got injured and the aircraft cabin saw significant damage, including a lavatory commode getting uprooted from its location. The overhead ceiling panel was found cracked or deformed at various places. Most of the passenger service unit panels were found dislocated or bent at various places. The overhead handrail was found broken and sealing panel found dislocated near the tenth row. The forward right side emergency exit handle was found broken.The cabin supervisor (head cabin crew) apprised the cockpit about the injuries suffered by the passengers and crew. The crew assessed the cabin situation and took the decision of continuing the flight to its destination Delhi and not diverting to the nearest en route airport.Following the report, AI said: “We acknowledge the release of the preliminary report by the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau and continue to extend our full cooperation to the investigation, including providing access to all relevant operational, maintenance and technical records. Safety remains Air India’s highest priority. Our pilots undergo rigorous training, regular proficiency checks, medical examinations and other regulatory assessments in accordance with applicable national and international requirements. Following the incident, Air India has started voluntary testing of 100% of its pilots as a further step to reinforce its safety-first approach.” “The airline maintains zero tolerance for any breach of safety, fitness or regulatory requirements,” Air India’s statement added.
Article Summary: Air india friday sacked the pilot-in-command of its badly rattled aug 4 phuket-delhi flight. Aircraft accident investigation bureau's preliminary report concluded the "pic was found non-negative for psycho-active substance" final report may reveal whether it happened due to something going wrong with the aircraft’s hardware or software.

NEW DELHI/MUMBAI: Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever on Friday said Europe had been slow to recognise the risks of becoming too dependent on other economies, admitting that Indian PM Narendra Modi had warned it about the problem much earlier but was not heard.De Wever, who was on a two-day visit to India to strengthen ties in trade, investment, technology and strategic cooperation, said India and Europe were now facing similar challenges as economic dependencies were increasingly being used as leverage. "We do not like dependencies becoming weaponised against us. You have lived this history. Your Prime Minister warned Europe about this long time ago already. But he was ignored. He wasn't listened to. We are listening now," De Wever said at a Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) event.Calling Europe's awakening "a bit late", De Wever said the region was now having the "right debates" about who it could work with in a world where major economic powers were moving in different directions.He said India was the most important partner for Europe among countries that believed in multilateralism and cooperation based on "respect and not force"."If India is not on the list, then you have missed something fundamental. India is on that list. It's number one," De Wever said.In an apparent reference to China, De Wever said Europe was seeking to reduce its dependence on "big economical powerhouses" that were moving away from rules-based cooperation. "I will not name them China," he said, adding that such a direction was not what Europe wanted.Speaking on the occasion, Union commerce minister Piyush Goyal said the India-EU FTA was a win-win for everyone. "It will open opportunities for farmers, start ups, women entrepreneurs, it has something for everyone. It's been deftly negotiated protecting sensitive sectors on both sides. It offers huge potential for both sides," he said.
Article Summary: Belgian pm said india and europe were now facing similar challenges. De wever was on a two-day visit to india to strengthen ties in trade, investment, technology and strategic cooperation. He said india was the most important partner for europe among countries that believed in multilateralism.

Article Title: 'Exceptionally rare': All 3 hydraulic systems of Air India Phuket-Delhi flight failed together
Article Text:
The hydraulic failure itself, the more immediate cause of the injuries onboard, unfolded within a five-second window. VT-EXO, an eight-year-old A320neo carrying 145 people, had just been cleared to climb from FL340 to FL360 after entering Kolkata Flight Information Region.

‘Triple hydraulic failure close to unthinkable’

MUMBAI: Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau's preliminary report has confirmed what pilots and engineers call an exceptionally rare event, the near-simultaneous loss of all three hydraulic systems on the A320neo aircraft at 36,000 feet. Hydraulic systems are the fluid-pressure circuits that physically move an aircraft's wing and tail surfaces. The green, blue and yellow systems dropped out within seconds of each other, triggering an autopilot disengagement, a stall warning and a brief altitude upset that injured 24 flyers.The accident occurred when the eight-year-old A320neo (VT-EXO) carrying 145 people had just been cleared to climb from 34,000 feet to 36,000 feet after entering the airspace controlled by Kolkata ATC. At 9:32:43am IST, within four seconds the flight control system detected loss of all the three hydraulic systems.In the next few seconds, the autopilot disengaged, a continuous repetitive chime sounded, and the stall warning triggered for two seconds. “The aircraft encountered altitude upset. Initially, it gained 372 ft and fell by 292 ft from its assigned 36,000 feet flight level during the event,” the report said.It did not give information on the cause of the triple hydraulic failure, nor did it put forth any safety recommendations for the A320 aircraft type. It said the investigation is in progress and hydraulic components, fluid samples and recorder data have been collected and are still being analysed.The critical information on the probable cause and contributory factors is likely to be released in the final report, expected to be published on or before Aug 4, 2027.In simple terms, hydraulic pressure is what physically moves an aircraft’s control surfaces, the ailerons on the wings that make it roll, the elevators on the tail that make it pitch up or down, and the rudder that makes it yaw left or right. Pilots move the stick and pedals, but it is hydraulic power that pushes the actual surfaces. An A320 carries three independent hydraulic circuits so that losing one, or even two, still leaves enough pressure to fly and manoeuvre the aircraft normally.“Losing all three at once is considered close to unthinkable, because the A320 has a triple-redundant hydraulic design which ensures no combination of failures can disable flight controls entirely. It is the kind of failure engineers cite alongside a handful of decades-old incidents involving other aircraft types, none of them an A320,” said a senior aircraft maintenance engineer. The notable total hydraulic loss events that occurred globally are the 1985 JAL 123 (Boeing 747), the 1989 United Airlines DC-10, and a DHL A300 that was hit by a missile over Baghdad in 2003.Following the triple hydraulic failure, the co-pilot, who was flying the aircraft, responded first to the upset before the captain took over the controls. Recovery was swift, the blue system came back within seconds, followed shortly by yellow and green, restoring normal flight control surfaces, the report said.
Article Summary: The accident occurred when the eight-year-old a320neo (vt-exo) carrying 145 people had just been cleared to climb. Within four seconds the flight control system detected loss of all the three hydraulic systems. Recovery was swift, the blue system came back within seconds, followed shortly by yellow and green.

Article Title: Coal stock at thermal plants plummets, 'critical' at 50 units
Article Text:

Of the 50 plants, 45 are based on domestic fuel

NEW DELHI: Coal stocks at thermal power plants across the country have fallen to less than half the recommended level, with 50 plants classified as having 'critically low' inventories as on Sept 2 amid high electricity demand and monsoon-led disruptions in supplies, Central Electricity Authority data showed.The plants, with a combined capacity of around 224 GW, had 28.2 million tonnes (MT) of coal as of Wednesday, 48% of the prescribed requirement of 58.7 MT. The available stock is equivalent to about nine days of coal requirement at 85% plant load factor, against the normal requirement of around 19 days.The plants classified as short on coal stocks have less than 25% of their normative inventories. Coal ministry officials, however, said all critical plants were being monitored by an inter-ministerial team of officials on a day-to-day basis and regular fuel supplies were being provided to them.Of the 50 plants, 45 are based on domestic fuel, four are designed for imported coal and one runs on washery rejects.A senior coal ministry official said, "Classification of a thermal power plant as critical is a routine monitoring parameter under norms laid down by CEA. It simply means closer tracking and priority action. These plants are not running out of supply."Though the normative coal requirement at power plants is calculated at 3.1 MT every day at 85% plant load factor, officials said the actual requirement is around 2.4 MT.The monsoon sees supply disruptions every year. The situation starts improving from Sept onwards as rains begin to recede.While the power ministry did not respond to requests for a reaction, sources said some coal-fired plants had been asked to defer scheduled maintenance to ensure continuity of electricity generation.
Article Summary: Coal stocks at thermal power plants across the country have fallen to less than half the recommended level. 50 plants classified as having 'critically low' inventories as on sept 2. Available stock is equivalent to about nine days of coal requirement at 85% plant load factor.

Article Title: RSS says of critics of Mohan Bhagwat’s UK trip: ‘Let them speak, we’re open to dialogue’

LONDON: The RSS shrugged off criticism by civil groups of its chief Dr Mohan Bhagwat’s UK trip, saying in a democracy differences of opinions are expected and “should not be taken as a shock”.The RSS head arrived in London on Sept 2 on the final leg of his three-city outreach RSS centenary tour, having just visited New York and Toronto on a “dialogue mission.”Hindus for Human Rights UK and several other campaign groups wrote an open letter to London mayor Sadiq Khan asking him to condemn the visit, pointing out New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani had done that.Labour PIO MP Nadia Whittome tabled a written parliamentary question asking the home office whether “the visit engages the commitment to block hate preachers and extremists from entering the UK”.“We are here for peace, integration and oneness and we are open for dialogue with everyone. In a democracy, it is very normal to raise different voices. We are engaging with those who wish to dialogue with us,” RSS head of media Sunil Ambekar said at a press briefing on Friday.“We are here to communicate what we are and how we think. We are very much open. We have nothing to hide. We expect a debate and exchange of thoughts. Let them speak.”On allegations the RSS was behind the 2022 Leicester riots, Ambekar said this was a “UK domestic issue”. “There is no question… RSS was not involved. Already people are finding out their legal options. Hindus are a peace-loving community.”He said there are a lot of “misconceptions” in the West. “Bharat is not a nation state political concept — it is a cultural concept. Hindutva is not like any religion — it’s a concept where there will be respect for all religious practices. That is Hindutva, and that is Bharat, so I think the trip will help to clear the ideas,” he said.A spokesperson for the London mayor said the mayor “does not have the power” to ban people from speaking. “London is proud to celebrate our diversity and intolerance has no place in our great city,” the spokesperson said.

Article Title: Work hard, own the world
Article Text:
may there always be enough for everyone.

Nediyon

Ulagalandhaan

“Madiyila Mannavan Eydhum Adialandhaan

Thaaya Dhellam Orungu.”

never underestimate the power of someone who appears unassuming. When the right moment comes, every Vamana may blossom into a Trivikrama.

Last week, I was in London and had a day to myself. I decided to visit the Sherlock Holmes Museum. Sherlock Holmes has always been a favourite character of mine. As is often the case in London, getting to the station, followed by two train rides. It was quite a journey, but entirely worth it.On my return, hunger took over. I was delighted when my host suggested a South Indian restaurant. I asked for a dosa .“Not available.” The only item on the menu was Onam sadhya.Of course, it was Onam.And suddenly, the absence of a dosa seemed like a blessing.A sadhya is not merely a meal. It is a celebration of abundance. Sitting in a corner of London, with thoran, erissery and jackfruit payasam before me, felt less like eating and more like being transported to heaven.Onam celebrates the annual return of King Mahabali to visit his people in Kerala. His reign is remembered as an age of prosperity, equality and generosity. The sadhya seems to embody the spirit of his kingdom:That thought took me to another story—that of Vamana , who became Trivikrama. The image at its core—the three cosmic strides of Vishnu—is much older. In the Rigveda, Vishnu is celebrated as the deity who takes three great steps across the universe. It is interesting that the names Rama and Krishna find little mention in the early scriptures, but Trivikrama is omnipresent; both in scriptures and literature, even in ancient Tamil literature. Sangam works such as Paripadal, Kalithogai and Perumpaanatrupadai evoke Vishnu asor—the One who measured the worlds.There is even an ancient tradition connecting the origin of the River Vaigai with this cosmic act. When Trivikrama raised his foot and pierced the upper worlds, Brahma is said to have washed that divine foot. The sacred water that flowed down towards Earth became associated with the Vaigai. Myth, landscape and poetry became woven together.Early Tamil poetry was deeply conscious of landscape, boundaries and celestial order. A God who could cross the limits of the universe with a single stride was a magnificent poetic image.And Thiruvalluvar, who rarely invokes deities directly, chose precisely this image in the Thirukkural .In the chapter on freedom from laziness, he says in Kural 610:“A king who is completely free from laziness will gain all that wasMeasured by the feet of Trivikrama.”The grandeur of the image is striking. Trivikrama measured the worlds with his feet; Valluvar transforms that into a metaphor for human effort. The energetic can reach whatever vastness the universe may contain. What seems beyond one’s grasp may become attainable when one refuses to be held back by indolence. And there is another thought in this transformation from Vamana to Trivikrama:And perhaps that was the unexpected journey I experienced at London: from Sherlock Holmes to an Onam sadhya, to Mahabali, and from Mahabali to Trivikrama; my friend and I travelled quite a lot for the dosa we didn’t get. My takeaway was; don’t be upset if you don’t get what you wanted: you may end up with much more!
Article Summary: A sadhya is not merely a meal. It is a celebration of abundance. Onam celebrates the annual return of king mahabali to visit his people in kerala. His reign is remembered as an age of prosperity, equality and generosity. That thought took me to another story—that of vamana, who became trivikrama.

NEW DELHI: Smoking increased the risk of death from any cause by 55% among people with diabetes, according to evidence reviewed in a new international consensus that calls for smoking cessation to be treated as an essential part of type-2 diabetes care. Experts say patients who smoke should be offered medicines, intensive behavioural counselling and regular follow-ups instead of being given a one-time "quit smoking" warning.The recommendations, published in Diabetes Research and Clinical Practice, represent the first dedicated international consensus on smoking cessation specifically for people with type-2 diabetes. They were developed by 35 experts from 13 countries, including Indian diabetes specialist Dr Anoop Misra.The consensus recommends varenicline as the first-line medicine where available, with nicotine replacement therapy or bupropion as alternatives when varenicline is unavailable or unsuitable. Medicines should be combined with structured, intensive behavioural support and repeated contact rather than brief counselling alone.The stronger approach reflects the added risk smoking poses to people with diabetes.A meta-analysis of 48 studies involving 1.13 million people found a 55% higher risk of death, while another study of about 130,000 people with diabetes found 48% higher overall mortality and 36% higher cardiovascular mortality among smokers.Doctors should review patients within two weeks of their quitting and again at four weeks, checking blood sugar, weight, blood pressure and medicines, as quitting can alter drug metabolism and sometimes require dose adjustments.Smoking is also linked to kidney damage in diabetics, with higher risks of albuminuria and diabetic nephropathy. A Japanese study of 2,490 people with type-2 diabetes found insulin resistance rose with cigarettes smoked per day and fell with time after quitting.Quitting, however, can be difficult. Some patients may not recognise the link between smoking and diabetes complications, while others fear weight gain or use cigarettes to cope with stress and anxiety. The experts recommend personalised quitting strategies and relapse prevention.
Article Summary: Smoking raises mortality risk by 55% for diabetics. Experts say patients who smoke should be offered medicines, intensive behavioural counselling and regular follow-ups. A meta-analysis of 48 studies involving 1.13 million people found a 55% higher risk of death.

Article Title: Jaishankar says India in touch with Russia, Ukraine to help end war

NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Friday said India has been in continuous touch with both Ukraine and Russia and is exploring whether ideas and suggestions can be developed to contribute to the mitigation and, ideally, the cessation of the conflict.Jaishankar made the remarks in Warsaw after holding talks with Poland's deputy Prime Minister and foreign minister Radosław Sikorski, a day after he met the top Ukrainian leadership in Kyiv.Addressing a joint press meet with Sikorski, Jaishankar said the two leaders discussed major global and regional issues, including the war in Ukraine, which is now in its fifth year.“The deputy Prime Minister and I also understandably discussed some major global and regional issues, notable among them is the war in Ukraine, now in its fifth year... I myself have just come here from Kyiv,” he said.Replying to a question, Jaishankar said India remained in touch with both sides.“What we are trying to do is to see if there are ideas and suggestions which can be developed in some way in which they will contribute to the mitigation, ideally, the cessation of the conflict,” he added.Jaishankar reiterated India's position that the conflict must end through dialogue and diplomacy.“India believes that endless war must give way to an end to war. These are wars without winners. Every additional day means more death, more destruction, more loss to the parties themselves, and more cost to the rest of the world,” he said.“Our efforts must therefore focus on promoting dialogue and diplomacy. We must each do what we can in whichever way we believe could be most effective and support the efforts of others to bring this conflict to an end. This is India's strong conviction, and we are acting on it,” he added.Responding to a question on India's purchases of Russian oil, Jaishankar said the solution to the conflict lay in negotiations rather than trade.“This war is not going to end... not because somebody chose to buy or not buy oil or alumina or fertilisers or metals and minerals. It will end when there is diplomacy, when there is dialogue and when there is negotiation. So, I think let's diagnose the problem right,” he said.A day earlier in Kyiv, Jaishankar had met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and foreign minister Andrii Sybiha and said India was ready to extend “any help in any manner” to help end the war.Following the meeting, Zelenskyy said he was “grateful to India for its commitment to ending this unjust war”.Jaishankar and Sikorski also discussed complex global challenges, including supply chain resilience and food, fuel and fertiliser security.The two ministers reviewed the progress of the India-Poland Joint Action Plan 2024-28, covering areas including trade and investment, space, digital technology, artificial intelligence, semiconductors, defence, education, shipping, mining and energy.Jaishankar also called on Polish President Karol Nawrocki and discussed the trajectory of the India-Poland Strategic Partnership, as well as the Ukraine conflict and developments in West Asia.

Article Title: ‘Developed countries must take lead': India calls for climate finance after Nepal flood
Article Text:
People walk next to damaged buildings following the deadly flash floods and mudslides in Devighat, Nuwakot district, Nepal (Picture credit: Reuters)

‘ Climate change is a common challenge’

India reiterates support for Nepal

Nepal clarifies compensation remarks

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs on Friday said developed countries must take the lead in reducing emissions and support developing nations through finance and technology transfer, reiterating India's position that climate action must be guided by the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities.The remarks by MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal came in the aftermath of the devastating flash floods in Nepal and amid questions over remarks concerning climate-related compensation from major economies, including India, China and the United States.Addressing the issue at a weekly media briefing, Jaiswal said India had consistently maintained that climate change was a shared challenge.“I understand that a clarification has also been issued by the Nepalese side. Having said that, let me say that India has consistently maintained that climate change is a common challenge, and action in this regard must be based on the principle of common differentiated responsibilities and respective capabilities,” he said.Jaiswal said countries historically responsible for emissions should take the lead in tackling the challenge and supporting developing nations.“Developed countries who historically are responsible for the emissions and have contributed overwhelmingly to the civil crisis, must take lead in reducing emissions and supporting developing countries by way of finance and technology transfer to meet this challenge,” the MEA spokesperson added.Jaiswal also said India had extended solidarity and support to Nepal following the tragedy and would continue to assist the country in its reconstruction and recovery efforts.“In the wake of this tragedy, we have extended our solidarity and support to the government and people of Nepal. As a close friend and partner, India responded promptly, and we will continue to support the reconstruction and recovery efforts in the country,” he said.Referring to Nepal Prime Minister Balen Shah's appreciation of India's assistance, Jaiswal said Prime Minister Narendra Modi had spoken to his Nepalese counterpart after the disaster and conveyed India's support.“We have seen that the Prime Minister of Nepal has thanked us for our support... our prime minister spoke to the Prime Minister of Nepal and conveyed that India stands shoulder to shoulder and extends all its support to Nepal in this time of crisis, and it will offer whatever help is required,” he said.Meanwhile, Nepal foreign minister Shisir Khanal clarified on Thursday that neither he nor the Nepalese government had sought climate-related compensation from India, China or the United States.“Neither I nor anyone in the ministry of foreign affairs or the government of Nepal has claimed or asked for compensation from India or any other country, including China or the United States,” Khanal told news agency ANI.Also read: Nepal minister clarifies 'compensation from world' remark after flash floods He said Nepal's appeal was for the global community to recognise climate change and its impact on the country.“Our call has been for the global community to look at this disaster from the perspective of climate change and the impact it's having in Nepal,” he added.Khanal also said India, China and Nepal shared environmental ecosystems and should work together to prepare for the impact of climate change in the Himalayas.He stressed the need to look beyond one-time disaster assistance and consider the longer-term effects of rising temperatures and climate change on communities.
Article Summary: India reiterates position that climate action must be guided by principle of common but differentiated responsibilities. Mea spokesperson randhir jaiswal said countries historically responsible for emissions should take the lead in tackling the challenge.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni on Friday thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi for congratulating her on becoming Italy’s longest continuously serving PM in the postwar period, saying the relationship between the two countries was “stronger than ever”.Sharing a post on X, Meloni said, “Thank you, dear Narendra Modi, for your words and for your friendship. The relationship between Italy and India is today stronger than ever.”“The Special Strategic Partnership that we launched during our last meeting is the recognition of the importance of this bond and of the will to unite the expertise of our Nations to create new opportunities for growth, seizing the extraordinary opportunities for collaboration that we have before us,” she said.“I am certain that Italy and India, together, will continue to strengthen the bond between our Continents as well, working side by side also to develop the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor,” she added.Meloni has served as Italy’s prime minister since October 22, 2022. On Thursday, after 1,413 consecutive days in office, she became the country’s longest continuously serving prime minister since World War II, surpassing the previous record held by former prime minister Silvio Berlusconi.Earlier in the day, PM Modi congratulated Meloni on the milestone, saying it reflected the trust and confidence of the Italian people in her leadership.“Congratulations to my friend Prime Minister Meloni on becoming the longest continuously serving Prime Minister in Italy's postwar history. This milestone is a reflection of the trust and confidence of the Italian people in her leadership,” PM Modi said in a post on X.He said Meloni’s friendship had played an important role in strengthening the India-Italy Special Strategic Partnership and that he looked forward to continuing close cooperation between the two countries.“My best wishes for her continued success in the years ahead,” the PM added.The friendship between PM Modi and Meloni has often attracted attention on social media, with users referring to the duo as “Melodi”, a combination of their surnames.The trend began in November 2023 when Meloni shared a selfie with PM Modi from the COP28 summit in Dubai with the caption “Good friends at COP28 #Melodi.” The hashtag quickly became popular, generating memes and viral posts.The two leaders again drew attention at the G7 summit in June, when Meloni joked about their online popularity. During the traditional group photograph, she told PM Modi, “Yeah, we are the most famous couple on Instagram.”The “Melodi” buzz also resurfaced during PM Modi’s visit to Rome last month, when he presented Meloni with a packet of Parle’s Melody chocolates in a playful reference to the trend.PM Modi himself became India’s longest continuously serving elected prime minister on June 10, 2026, after completing 4,399 consecutive days in office.

NEW DELHI: So, who does Sonia Gandhi’s controversial memoir ‘Belonging’ belong to? HarperCollins India has stepped in to publish the Congress leader’s memoir, ending weeks of uncertainty over who would carry the domestic edition after Penguin Random House India (PRHI) exited the deal over some changes to the text. The book will hit Indian shelves on November 10, 2026 — the same day as its international release.Billed as one of the most anticipated political memoirs in recent years, Belonging is described as a personal account of love, identity, duty and belonging, offering an insider's perspective on India's political journey through Gandhi's own eyes.The HarperCollins announcement comes on the heels of a public controversy over PRHI's departure from the project, which Congress leaders have framed as an act of political censorship. Party leader Ashok Gehlot alleged that pressure had been exerted on Penguin to edit out sections dealing with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the RSS, and China's occupation of Indian territory during Modi's tenure, calling the episode a "murder of democracy.Penguin pushed back on that framing, maintaining that it retained the right to fact-check manuscripts and suggest edits to authors, and said it remained open to publishing the book.The company had earlier this year also halted distribution of cartoonist Joe Sacco's The Once and Future Riot, about the Muzaffarnagar riots — a decision critics have pointed to as part of a pattern.Adding a layer of intrigue to the row was the fact that Alfred A. Knopf, the memoir's American publisher, is itself a Penguin Random House imprint — raising the question, as Gehlot put it, of why a version cleared for global release would need alteration for Indian readers. "What is the reason, or what pressure is there that what is being published across the world cannot be published in India?" he asked.
Article Summary: Harpercollins to publish former congress chief sonia gandhi's memoir after penguin backs out. The book will hit indian shelves on november 10, 2026 — the same day as its international release. Belonging is described as a personal account of love, identity, duty and belonging.
